subject: Commit gap investigation + adaptive tier proposal
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jules Martin <jules.martin@luminary.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@luminary.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Commit gap investigation + adaptive tier proposal

Hi Jules — looping you in and copying Karthik and Ben from our Renewals/Capacity team.

TL;DR: We identified a Q2-to-Q3 commit gap for Luminary's account and put together a short proposal with three options to avoid overages while preserving unit economics. See attachments for the raw month-by-month token breakdown and the latency/throughput snapshot from last week.

What we saw:
- Committed: 12,000,000 tokens/mo (current committed tier)
- Actual forecast for June (post-marketing push): 18,200,000 tokens/mo -> ~6.2M token shortfall
- Peak concurrency aligned with a new marketing campaign will increase token burstiness (20–30% higher peak tokens/hour).

Risk: Without adjustment, Luminary will incur ~30% overage spend in June relative to committed pricing.

Three pragmatic options (fastest to slowest):
1) Short-term burst credits + temporary headroom (30-day): Redwood provides a one-time burst credit to smooth the immediate surge. Good for one-off campaigns, keeps contract unchanged.
2) Adaptive tier (recommended): Convert current commit to a flexible 12→18M blended commitment for the next 3 months with a tiered step-up. This preserves most of your unit discount and removes immediate overage risk. We also recommend a modest 10% uplift to reserve headroom after month 3.
3) Term extension + rate reset: Extend contract 6 months and increase commit to 20M at a lower per-token rate. Best long-term unit economics but requires procurement lead time.

Questions for you before we pick a path:
- How fixed is the June campaign timeline? Is the spike concentrated in weeks 1–2 or spread out?
- Do you want us to route traffic to a higher-capacity variant during the campaign (there are latency tradeoffs)?
- Procurement contact copied — if you want #3 we can draft a change order and send a DocuSign placeholder.

Next step: propose a 30-min sync today or tomorrow. Karthik — can you attach a quick blended-price calc? Ben — can you confirm whether dedicated autoscale can be turned on for Luminary's org this week?

Attachments: q2-usage-breakdown.csv (CSV, 45KB), projected-peak-forecast.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB), model-latency-report.pdf (PDF, 600KB)

Thanks,

— Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — really appreciate the quick analysis. Some context from our side: the June spike is tied to a product launch scheduled for 6/7; the majority of traffic should be concentrated in the first two weeks of June (heavy bursts during daytime PST). We do anticipate ongoing elevated usage through July but not as sharp.

Quick notes:
- We prefer to avoid a long-term term extension unless unit economics are materially better — procurement will push back otherwise.
- If the adaptive tier preserves ~85–90% of current unit discount, that's attractive.
- Burst credits would help patch the first two weeks while we finalize a short-term commit.

procurement@luminary.ai — if we go with option #2 for 3 months, can you accelerate approvals? We may need an abbreviated PO.

Happy to do a 30-min call at 11:30am PT today.

Subject: Re: Commit gap investigation + adaptive tier proposal

Adding the preliminary numbers requested. See quick calc below (rounded):

Baseline: committed 12M tokens/mo at $0.90 per 1k tokens (effective after discounts)
Forecast: 18.2M tokens/mo
Gap: 6.2M tokens -> if billed at list overage $1.40 per 1k => incremental cost ~ $8,680 for the month (6.2M/1k * $1.40)

Option economics (30-day period, example):
- Burst credit (one-time): We can offer $6k credit to cover the initial burst; Luminary pays any overage beyond that. Pros: fastest. Cons: doesn't change long-term risk.
- Adaptive 3-month blended: convert to 15M committed for month 1, 18M for month 2, 18M for month 3 with a 10% headroom reserved. Blended effective price ~ $1.00 per 1k tokens vs current $0.90 — net additional $1.2k in month 1 compared to committing 12M and paying overage. But avoids the unpredictable overage spikes and simplifies forecasting.
- Term + rate reset (6 months at 20M): effective price could drop to $0.80 per 1k — better long-term, needs PO/Procurement sign-off and 7–10 day lead time.

Recommendation: take Adaptive 3-month blended (option #2) and include a $6k burst credit to smooth week 1. This gives Luminary short-term protection and buys procurement time for a longer commit if they want.

Ben — on autoscale: we can enable dedicated autoscale for Luminary's endpoint. For the campaign window (6/7–6/14) we can add an extra node pool that will keep 20% extra headroom. Ops will need a thumbs-up by EOD to schedule.

Karthik
Senior Renewals Analyst | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — aligning on next steps below so we have a single source of truth after the call at 11:30: 

1) Short-term: Redwood to apply $6,000 burst credit to Luminary's June invoice (covers initial campaign window).
2) Medium-term (recommended): Start adaptive 3-month blended commit: 15M / 18M / 18M months 1–3. Finance will run the blended SOW tonight and route a short addendum.
3) Autoscale: Ben to enable dedicated autoscale pool for 6/7–6/14 (20% extra headroom). Ops to confirm config by EOD tomorrow.
4) Procurement: procurement@luminary.ai — Redwood will send a DocuSign change order (placeholder link below) for the addendum; please advise on PO timing.

Action owners and due dates:
- Redwood Finance (Karthik): send blended SOW/addendum draft — by Tue 5/4 EOD
- Ops (Ben): confirm autoscale node pool config — by Tue 5/4 5pm PT
- Luminary Procurement: confirm PO or acceptance of DocuSign addendum — target Wed 5/5

I'll send the DocuSign link and the HubSpot deal note after this thread. Thanks again — looks like a clean path to avoid overage and preserve decent unit economics for Luminary.

Best,
